Named Mr. Georgia Basketball by the [[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]][http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crittenton_javaris00.html Javaris Crittenton bio], ramblinwreck.cstv.com, accessed [[February 13]], [[2007]]. }} '''Javaris Crittenton''' (born [[December 31]] [[1987]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[college basketball]] player for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]]. He is currently in his [[college freshman|freshman]] year. Standing 6 ft 4 in and weighing 194 [[pound (mass)|lbs]], Crittenton plays [[point guard]] for the Yellow Jackets. Crittenton is projected by major media outlets such as [[ESPN]] to be a likely first-round draft pick in the [[2007 NBA Draft]] should he decide to leave school early.[http://insider.espn.go.com/nbadraft/draft/tracker/player?playerId=19027&draftyear=2007&action=login&appRedirect=http%3a%2f%2finsider.espn.go.com%2fnbadraft%2fdraft%2ftracker%2fplayer%3fplayerId%3d19027%26draftyear%3d2007 Javaris Crittenton profile], espn.com, accessed [[February 12]], [[2007]]. ==Biography== ===Early life and high school=== Crittenton was born to Sonya Dixon in [[Atlanta, Georgia]].[http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/player/profile?playerId=31615 Javaris Crittendon], espn.com, accessed [[February 13]], [[2007]]. one younger sister, Shaniya Lee. Crittenton grew up in a single-parent household and was raised by his mother.[http://www.ajc.com/sports/content/sports/highschool/stories/0618crittenton.html Athete of the Year-Boy's Basketball SACA's Javaris Crittenton: 'I could never get you to put that ball down'], ''[[Atlanta Journal Constitution]]'', accessed [[February 13]], [[2007]]. As a child, Crittenton played basketball obsessively; he practiced on a children's basketball hoop he got for [[Christmas]] when he was five years old every day until it finally broke. In later years his mother stated that she often had a hard time getting him to stop playing and practicing basketball. Despite this obsession Crittenton was a good student as a child. Crittenton attended [[Southwest Atlanta Christian Academy]], where as a high school [[tenth grade|sophomore]] he played alongside [[Dwight Howard]]. Crittenton and Howard led Southwest Atlanta to the [[Georgia High School Association|GHSA]] class A state championship that season. Howard would later go on to be the first overall pick in the [[2004 NBA Draft]] after turning professional directly out of high school.[http://www.nba.com/draft2004/board.html 2004 NBA Draft], nba.com, accessed [[February 22]], [[2007]]. As a [[eleventh grade|junior]] Crittenton averaged 28.4 [[point (basketball)|points]], 7.5 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 8.2 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. He led Southwest Atlanta to the GHSA class A state final again where they lost, finishing the season as the runner-up. As a [[twelfth grade|senior]] Crittenton averaged 29 points, 9 assists, and 7 rebounds and led Southwest Atlanta to the GHSA class A state championship. Following the season he was named a [[McDonald's All American]].He was also named Mr. Georgia Basketball. Crittenton was an exceptional student in high school who had a 3.5 [[grade (education)#United States|GPA]] and was a member of the Future Business Leaders of America and the Senior Beta Club. After being courted by several colleges Crittenton ultimately chose local Georgia Tech, in part to allow his mother and little sister to be able to attend his games. ===College=== While at Georgia Tech, Crittenton has excelled and is considered a team leader, a rare honor for a freshman.[[Associated Press]]. [http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/mld/ledgerenquirer/sports/colleges/georgia_tech/16643508.htm Tech's Crittenton emerges as a leader], ledger-enquirer.com, accessed [[February 13]], [[2007]]. Tech coach [[Paul Hewitt]] urged Crittenton to take over a leadership role on the team after his play in several games in February 2007. He recorded a career high of 29 points in a [[February 13]], [[2007]] game against [[Florida State Seminoles|Florida State]].Associated Press.
